title: Trump Administration Divide on China Policy Breaks Into Public View
summary: The airing of a fight over advanced A.I. chips shows how much the Nvidia scandal has deepened fissures inside the government, just as President Trump heads to a critical meeting with his Chinese counterpart.

President Trump headed on Monday for a trip to Asia to meet President Xi Jinping of China with his administration openly divided over how hard to squeeze that country on artificial intelligence technology.


Mr. Trump noted before he left that he has not wanted to make moves that “insult China.”


The public airing of the fight over China policy inside Mr. Trump’s cabinet shows how much[the fallout of the Nvidia scandal](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/15/us/politics/nvidia-trump-huang-china-xi.html) has deepened fissures inside the government, forcing into view a debate about how the United States should reckon with Beijing.


Mr. Trump, who is due to meet Mr. Xi and President Vladimir V. Putin of Russia at a summit in the Chinese tech hub of Shenzhen this week, has struggled to balance national security concerns about America’s most powerful rival against his desire to prop up Nvidia’s chips business and avoid another trade war with Mr. Xi.


Those tensions were center stage on Monday as the president[acknowledged](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/16/us/politics/bessent-lutnick-china.html) that Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick had been at odds over how hard to crack down on a loophole that has allowed China to access advanced A.I. chips through data centers in other countries.


“One wants to be friendly with China, and one wants to have a blowup with China,” Mr. Trump said of his two cabinet secretaries, speaking to reporters on the South Lawn before leaving for Asia. “Both are acceptable, but they’re different views.”


The debate intensified with the[resignation](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/12/technology/nvidia-jensen-huang.html) last week of Nvidia’s chief executive, Jensen Huang, after revelations that he had two extramarital affairs, including with[Alice Huang](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/10/technology/alice-huang-megaspeed-nvidia-jensen-huang.html) , a woman whom U.S. officials have identified as a Chinese intelligence asset.
